clue.text: Non-U composition rejected after single mistake

indicators.note: after places the turned piece behind the word for single

parts.note: single means sole, as in a sole survivor

indicators.note: rejected means the shortened word is thrown back, read right to left
Non-U tells us to drop the letter U from the word for composition

parts.note: a musical composition is music

explanation.surface: A piece of writing deemed socially vulgar is turned down because of a single error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Non-U' looks like the old British class label for vulgar usage, which fits a solecism, but here it simply removes U from MUSIC to leave MSIC; 'rejected' turns that to CISM.
explanation.definitionFit: A solecism is a grammatical blunder or breach of etiquette, so it is a kind of error.

clue.text: Line I'd included in hymn

indicators.note: included in means the short form goes inside the verb for hymn

parts.note: to hymn is to sing praises
the contraction I'd gives the letters ID

explanation.surface: A reference to a line is slipped into a hymn.
explanation.definitionFit: A siding is a short railway line off the main track.

clue.text: Regimental dance

parts.note: names a nineteenth-century square dance that shares its name with a cavalry regiment armed with lances

explanation.definitionFit: The lancers was a quadrille, a ballroom dance, and Lancers are also cavalry regiments.

clue.text: Riders all getting into taxi at London landmark

indicators.note: getting into puts the word all straight after the taxi, as a passenger climbs in
at joins the landmark onto the end

parts.note: a cab is a taxi
the statue known as Eros stands at Piccadilly Circus in London

explanation.surface: Horsemen all pile into a cab at Piccadilly Circus.
explanation.walkthrough: EROS is the popular name for the winged statue at Piccadilly Circus, central London.
explanation.definitionFit: Caballeros are Spanish gentlemen on horseback, so they are riders.

clue.text: Accedes to palmist's request and reveals all?

definitions.meaning: a fortune-teller asks to see your palm, and you hold it out
figuratively, to disclose one's intentions, as a card player lays cards face up

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to disclose one's plans, and literally means to hold out a palm for reading.

clue.text: Politicians were framing reply

indicators.note: framing says the two clue words enclose the solution within their run of letters, as a frame holds a picture

explanation.surface: Members of parliament were plotting how to respond.
explanation.definitionFit: An answer is a response, so the noun reply is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Woman who hasn't been recognised as artist?

parts.note: not recognised means no, the honour was refused
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A woman whose paintings never won official recognition.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, Royal Academician, is a member of the Royal Academy of Arts in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Nora is a woman's name, so it stands for any woman in crossword terms.

clue.text: Bird having feathers mostly protected by fleecy stuff

indicators.note: protected by means the shortened feathers sit inside the fleece

parts.note: wool is the fleecy coat of sheep

indicators.note: mostly means drop the last letter

parts.note: down is soft fine feathers

explanation.surface: A bird has its plumage mostly wrapped in fleece.
explanation.definitionFit: The wood owl is a species of owl, such as the tawny owl, so it is a bird.

clue.text: Singer's revolutionary launch

parts.note: red is a communist, a revolutionary
a start is a launch or beginning

explanation.surface: A vocalist's career gets off to a radical beginning.
explanation.definitionFit: The redstart is a songbird, and crosswords often call birds singers.

clue.text: Karate expert's book (abbreviated version)

indicators.note: abbreviated version asks for the short form under which this Old Testament book is cited

parts.note: Daniel is a book of the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A guide to karate grades is published in a condensed edition.
explanation.walkthrough: Bible books have standard short forms, and Daniel is cited as Dan.
explanation.definitionFit: In martial arts a dan is a black-belt grade, and by extension a person holding it is an expert.

clue.text: Trouble about first of rules introduced to outlaw union

indicators.note: about means the word for trouble goes round the letter taken from rules

parts.note: to trouble someone is to bother them

indicators.note: first of picks out the opening letter of the word rules

parts.note: hood is short for hoodlum, a gangster or outlaw; introduced to just joins it on

explanation.surface: Reformers make trouble by imposing rules on a banned trade union.
explanation.definitionFit: A brotherhood is an association or fellowship, especially a trade union in the US.

clue.text: Lose match if getting in a state about provisional result

indicators.note: getting in a state means becoming agitated, so the letters are disordered

parts.note: re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A team that might lose the game panics about the score at the interval.
explanation.definitionFit: The half-time score is the result so far at the interval, provisional until the game ends.

clue.text: Unnecessarily secretive on what Christmas tree bears

indicators.note: on means one piece is placed after the other

parts.note: a fir tree carries needles rather than leaves
sly means furtive or secretive

explanation.surface: Someone is pointlessly hush-hush about what is hanging on the Christmas tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something needlessly means doing it without need, that is unnecessarily.

clue.text: Scream, noise made by 7

definitions.meaning: a scream is something hilarious, as in what a scream
7-down is a kind of owl, and an owl's call is this sound

explanation.definitionFit: A hoot is both a very funny thing or person and the cry of an owl.

clue.text: Holidaymaker caught a reveller cuddling girl

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: cuddling means the reveller holds the girl inside

parts.note: a raver is a partygoer or reveller
Ann is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A tourist is caught as a partygoer hugs a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A caravanner takes holidays in a caravan, so is a holidaymaker.

clue.text: For instance, sea bird seen here?

definitions.text: For instance, sea bird seen here?

parts.note: as means for instance, as in sports such as tennis
a tern is a sea bird

explanation.surface: Asking where one might spot a gull-like bird, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: sea birds often follow behind a ship, where a terns could be seen.
explanation.definitionFit: Astern means behind a ship, which is where sea birds are typically seen trailing a vessel.

clue.text: One who complains, getting stuck at back of slowest truck

indicators.note: getting stuck at puts the complainer immediately after that final letter
back of picks the final letter of the word slowest

parts.note: a railer is one who rails, i.e. complains bitterly

explanation.surface: A moaner gets stuck behind the slowest lorry on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A trailer is a wheeled vehicle hauled behind another, a kind of truck.

clue.text: There's value in song being musical

indicators.note: in places the word for value inside the word for song

parts.note: a carol is a song
use means value, as in of no use

explanation.surface: A song has worth by virtue of being melodic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'musical' reads as an adjective; it is the noun, the Rodgers and Hammerstein show.
explanation.definitionFit: Carousel is a Rodgers and Hammerstein stage musical.

clue.text: Difficult road with sharp bend — that's nothing, in Oz!

indicators.note: in means the three pieces go inside the abbreviation for Australia

parts.note: Oz is slang for Australia, abbreviated AUS
a U-bend or U-turn is a hairpin, so U is a sharp bend
O looks like zero, i.e. nothing

explanation.surface: Driving an outback road with a hairpin bend is hard, but Australians shrug it off.
explanation.definitionFit: Arduous means demanding great effort, so it is a synonym of difficult.

clue.text: US city is almost too much for Frenchman and Italian

indicators.note: almost drops the last letter

parts.note: de trop is French for too much

explanation.surface: An American city is a bit excessive for a Frenchman and an Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: Detroit is a city in Michigan, United States.

clue.text: Laymen treated in despicable fashion

indicators.note: treated suggests the letters are processed and so reworked into new order

explanation.surface: Ordinary people were handled shabbily.
explanation.definitionFit: Meanly means shabbily or contemptibly, an adverb matching in despicable fashion.

clue.text: Attack oafish tree-hugger?

indicators.note: hugger means the oaf wraps around the tree

parts.note: an oafish person is a lout
the ash is a tree

explanation.surface: Someone mocks a clumsy environmentalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tree-hugger' looks like an eco-protester, but the hyphenated word splits into the tree and the one doing the hugging.
explanation.definitionFit: To lash out is to attack suddenly and violently.

clue.text: Journalist from Wapping wearing black blazer

indicators.note: wearing means the word for black has the journalist on, i.e. around

parts.note: jet is a deep black

indicators.note: from Wapping means a Cockney accent that drops the opening H

parts.note: a hack is a journalist

explanation.surface: A newspaperman from Wapping has a black blazer on.
explanation.walkthrough: Wapping is in London's East End, where Cockney speech drops H; it is also where The Times was printed, so a hack is apt.
explanation.definitionFit: A blazer is a kind of jacket.

clue.text: Swear word is old hat, curiously

indicators.note: curiously signals that the letters appear in an odd, rearranged order

explanation.surface: Bad language has become passe, strangely enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swear word' looks like a curse, but an oath is also a solemn sworn promise, i.e. a word one swears.
explanation.definitionFit: An oath is a solemn sworn pledge and also a profanity, so either sense of swear word fits.

clue.text: It kept prisoners of war, we're told, secure for the most part

indicators.note: we're told means the word for of war is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: martial means relating to war

indicators.note: for the most part drops the last letter of the word for secure

parts.note: to seal is to secure or close tightly

explanation.surface: A prisoner-of-war camp, by all accounts, was largely secure.
explanation.walkthrough: The Marshalsea was a notorious debtors' prison in Southwark, London, closed in 1842 and familiar from Dickens.
explanation.definitionFit: The Marshalsea was a London prison, so it literally kept prisoners.

clue.text: School report written up

indicators.note: written up in a down clue means read from bottom to top

parts.note: a note is a brief written report

explanation.surface: A school report is filed.
explanation.walkthrough: ETON College is the famous English public school near Windsor.
explanation.definitionFit: Eton is a leading English public school.

clue.text: Crook shot … wounded … silenced

indicators.note: crook means bent or twisted, so the letters are distorted

explanation.surface: A gangster is shot and wounded and goes quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crook' looks like the criminal who did the shooting; here it means bent, signalling the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: To be shouted down is to be silenced by louder voices.

clue.text: Nose of certain wines heavy drinker hasn't opened

indicators.note: hasn't opened means the drinker lacks the opening letter

parts.note: a soak is a heavy drinker

explanation.surface: A wine buff notes the aroma that a heavy drinker never bothers to uncork.
explanation.definitionFit: Wines aged in casks carry a woody aroma, which tasters describe as oak on the nose.

clue.text: Came down to some boring recital

parts.note: to light on something is to come down on it, past tense lit
any means some, as in have you any

explanation.surface: Matters were reduced to a tedious recitation.
explanation.definitionFit: A litany is a long repetitive prayer or list, hence a tedious recital.

clue.text: A niggle about rubbish university qualification

indicators.note: about means the word for niggle wraps around the word for rubbish

parts.note: to eat at someone is to niggle or worry them
grot is British slang for rubbish or junk

explanation.surface: A small complaint about a worthless degree.
explanation.walkthrough: An aegrotat is a degree awarded to a student too ill to sit the exams.
explanation.definitionFit: An aegrotat is a pass degree granted at a university on medical grounds, so it is a qualification.
